missionPremise: packages/adapters/src/hydrology/noaaAtlas14.ts parsePfdsDepthTable matches a `<tr><td>` HTML table, and the live HDSC endpoint (hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/new/cgi_readH5.py) no longer returns HTML — it returns a JavaScript array-literal payload (`result = 'values'; quantiles = [['0.458', ...], ...];`). The parser therefore never matches, and the call paths that depend on it serve a number the parser did not produce while the payload carries a NOAA Atlas 14 citation. Basis: the row's acceptance clause in OPS-17 G-165 plus ENFORCEMENT.md's opening defect class (a fabricated value presented as an earned one). Confirmed independently below on 2026-09-18, not inherited from G-125's 2026-09-14 reading.
completionPredicate: parsePfdsDepthTable parses the live HDSC payload shape and returns a 100-yr 24-hr depth that VARIES WITH LOCATION — proven by two points whose true Atlas 14 depths genuinely differ (Bastrop 12.6 in, El Paso 4.70 in) returning those two different values; a payload the parser does not understand REFUSES (throws a typed refusal) rather than returning an empty/partial map, so no caller can read `noaa-atlas14` over a number the parser did not produce; and every surviving fallback is (a) named with its reason, (b) counted, and (c) marked on the read. Falsified by: the two points returning the same depth; OR a perturbed payload returning a value instead of refusing; OR any surviving code path that emits a NOAA citation over an unparsed number.
scopeBasis: hauska-engine only, no writes in doc_repo beyond the three named close artifacts, no writes in smartcity-dashboards / smartcity-os, FAN-DEPTH 0. In scope: noaaAtlas14.ts (the parser + the fetch wrapper's failure signal), rainfallForcing.ts (the invented `?? 4` under a NOAA kind), the one route consumer of that kind (services/engine-api/src/routes/hydrology.ts), and the study/PDF provenance strings that cite NOAA for a default. Out of scope and named: (1) `_design/smartcity-flood-study/` — doc_repo, another row, deliberately left failing per G-164; NOT touched; (2) the pre-existing engine-core suite failures, named as inherited below, NOT chased; (3) the Cotality REST rail — dead per the canon preamble, untouched; (4) any change to the Atlas 14 row/column semantics beyond what the labeled sibling endpoint cross-validates.

liveEndpointGroundTruth.identityCorrection: CORRECTED 2026-09-18T22:35Z, after this checkpoint was first written. A raw-body hash is NOT a stable identity for this endpoint: the payload embeds `pyRunTime = <float>`, which differs on every call (measured: two consecutive fetches, 5073 vs 5074 bytes, different sha256, the byte difference confined to that field). The stable identity is `quantilesLiteralSha256`, which is the matrix the parser consumes; the committed fixture `packages/adapters/src/hydrology/__fixtures__/pfds-bastrop-tx-2026-09-18.pfds.txt` hashes to d77aa09c... for its quantiles literal, matching the probe's live capture exactly.
liveEndpointGroundTruth.matrixShape: quantiles is 19 rows x 10 columns. Rows are DURATIONS in NOAA's printed order (5-min, 10-min, 15-min, 30-min, 60-min, 2-hr, 3-hr, 6-hr, 12-hr, 24-hr, 2-day, 3-day, 4-day, 7-day, 10-day, 20-day, 30-day, 45-day, 60-day); columns are ARI in years (1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000). The payload carries NO labels for either axis.
liveEndpointGroundTruth.axisSemanticsBasisKept: Cross-validated 2026-09-18 against the LABELED sibling endpoint https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/new/fe_text.csv (same lat/lon/type/data/units/series, 301-redirect followed). Its header row is verbatim `by duration for ARI (years):, 1,2,5,10,25,50,100,200,500,1000` and its row labels are verbatim `5-min:`, `10-min:`, ... The `24-hr:` row's values are IDENTICAL to quantiles row index 9, for both probe points. The unlabeled matrix's index order is therefore not assumed, it is anchored to a labeled second derivation.
liveEndpointGroundTruth.trueDepthsForThisRow: 100-yr 24-hr: Bastrop 12.6 in; El Paso 4.70 in. These two numbers are the post-fix expected values.

liveEndpointGroundTruth.whyOtherResultStatesMatter: `result` is a clean three-way discriminator the payload itself carries: 'values' (real data), 'null' (inside the grid, no values — e.g. water), 'none'/'error' (outside every Atlas 14 project area). That is the mechanism by which a fallback for a genuinely-uncovered location can be NAMED with NOAA's own reason instead of being indistinguishable from a parse failure. Before this probe, nothing in the repo read `result`.

defectHalf1Confirmed: Live payload is a JavaScript array-literal, not HTML. VERBATIM, TODAY: `result = 'values';` / `quantiles = [['0.458', '0.538', ...], ...]`. Read 2026-09-18T22:15:33.596Z, HTTP 200, 5073 bytes, sha256 318519478fec... Re-ran the curl rather than trusting the 2026-09-14 reading, per the dispatch.
defectHalf2Confirmed: parsePfdsDepthTable's regex is /<tr[^>]*>\s*<td[^>]*>\s*(\d+)\s*<\/td>\s*<td[^>]*>\s*([\d.]+)\s*<\/td>/gi (noaaAtlas14.ts:30-31). Run against both live payloads it returns an EMPTY Map (mapSize 0, depth100yr null) — measured, not reasoned. It is not that it matches the wrong rows; it matches nothing at all.

preFixViolation.reportThisPrecisely: The dispatch says the fallback is 'Bastrop's 9.5in regional default ... presented as a measured value, with rainfallSource reading noaa-atlas14'. MEASURED, the two paths fail differently and the difference is worth stating rather than smoothing: (a) the STUDY path serves 9.5 with rainfallSource='default' and a detail string that names NOAA Atlas 14 Volume 11 (Texas) as the regional default — so it is MARKED as a default but still cites NOAA at asserted confidence on the sheet (pdf/flood-drainage.ts:1113 'NOAA Atlas 14 Volume 11 (Texas) regional default' with CONFIDENCE.asserted); (b) the ROUTE path (POST /rainfall-forcing, services/engine-api) serves a hardcoded 4 inches for every point, under kind='noaa-atlas-14', with designStormCount 0 — an invented number wearing the earned citation, and hydrology.ts:233 then classifies it as NOT degraded (okCoverage), so the invented number is also reported as full coverage. (b) is the sharper site and the dispatch did not name it; it was found by running the code, not by reading the prose.
preFixViolation.dispatchMechanismPartlyStale: With designStorms empty, resolveStudyRainfall's noaa-atlas14 branch is unreachable (it is gated on finding a 100-yr storm), so the study path has been reading 'default' — not a mis-cited 'noaa-atlas14' — since G-125 landed 2026-09-14. The mis-citation the row describes is live on the route path. Recorded so the fix targets the measured mechanism, not the narrated one.

environmentalDeviation: Node fetch from this workstation to hdsc.nws.noaa.gov fails TLS with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE (unable to verify the first certificate). Same class of deviation the p332-etj-panel CP1 recorded for cortex-api. Resolved by running the probe with NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca (Node 24's system trust store), NOT by disabling verification and NOT by installing a CA. curl.exe on the same machine reached the endpoint without special handling, which is why the raw payload captures are curl-based. Recorded rather than worked around silently.
